newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines not seen buying wheat as prices high.
newsitem.headline: Philippines not seen buying wheat as prices high.

text.p: Philippine grains importers are expected to stay out of the market in the coming week due to high wheat prices in the United States and other alternative markets, Manila traders said on Friday.
Major Philippine millers have ample supply for the month, said one trader in a U.S.-based commodity house.
"But if prices soften next week we can buy for our January requirement," an official in one of the country's largest Philippine mills said.
Rising wheat prices in the U.S. have forced local millers in the past few days to buy from alternative markets like Canada, Australia and Argentina, which all offer lower prices.
"We may see more purchases from other countries like Canada, Australia and Argentina if U.S. prices don't soften for the rest of the year," said an executive in a Philippine flour mill.
The Philippines buys an average of two million tonnes of wheat a year year, the bulk of it from the U.S.

Local buyers have been purchasing between five and 10 percent of their requirements from Canada in the past few years while Australia accounts for a meagre two percent of imports, the flour mill official said.

"The 20,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat bought by RFM Corp and Universal Robina Corp on December 5 from (commodity house) Toepfer was the country's first Argentine wheat purchase," a trader involved in the deal said.
The wheat was for January 1997 shipment, the trader added.
Philippine millers also received additional offers for 70,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for their January 1997 requirements, traders said.

On December 7, two other Philippine companies bought a total of 35,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat through commodity house Continental Grains at an average $178 a tonne FOB Vancouver for January delivery, traders said.
RFM also bought another 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on Wednesday for January shipment, they said.
The Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing price of hard flour in Metro Manila was 290 pesos per 25-kilo bag and 260 pesos for soft flour.
The Philippines is expected to import more rice and corn next year to meet rising demand.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said he expected the country to import between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of rice next year and up to 500,000 tonnes of corn for animal feed.
Escudero said rice imports will probably be brought in by the end of the second quarter in 1997 and just ahead of the seasonally lean third quarter when supplies are normally tight.

The state-agency National Food Authority said some 67,500 tonnes of yellow corn imported from the U.S. had arrived in the country in the past three weeks. Three other ships, carrying a total of 79,999 tonnes, are scheduled to arrive during the remainder of this year.
The average farm-gate price of white corn dropped to 6.40 pesos a kg this week from the previous 6.45 while yellow corn was pegged at 6.40 pesos a kg from 6.43.
Average retail price of white corn rose to 11.41 pesos a kg from 11.17 pesos while yellow corn slid to 11.13 pesos a kg from 10.82 pesos.
